experience.summary: Delivered four agents for engineering, product planning and project management teams in Shanghai, serving around 500 internal users in total.
highlights: Built agents for connector selection, competitive analysis, PRD generation and review, and black-box testing, addressing cost-reduction briefs from three departments.

Connector selection: an 8.5k-line Python system using Flask, LangChain and MongoDB. An LLM decomposes requests into exact, fuzzy and range queries across five product collections with automatic field mapping. Engineer-confirmed results become reusable knowledge-base templates. Shipped eight releases, including a dataset migration and a simpler fallback path.
Competitive analysis: an LLM-driven crawler collects public vehicle-owner reviews into MongoDB. Six chapter-level agents form a pipeline that produces a structured, evidence-backed report.

AUT: a 3.1k-line Python black-box testing tool. Playwright locates the chat interface, captures live API calls and produces replayable request templates, with manual handoff for CAPTCHA, SSO and MFA. Staged load tests stop on success-rate, error-rate and p95 thresholds; probes check prompt injection, cross-session leakage and output stability.

Measured the connector agent at 100% success and 14.2-second p95 with 20 concurrent users. At 500 concurrent users, success fell to 94.9%, with 51 of 1,000 responses empty or malformed. These measurements identify a degradation point, not a universal performance guarantee.

experience.summary: Built vision algorithms for a special-operations competency examination system in Zhengzhou, owning deployment across three production lines.
highlights: Worked on an examination system with the municipal emergency-management bureau. Four to five synchronized cameras assess procedural compliance and completeness. The system ran live exams every working day for over a month; I owned three production lines and defined annotation standards with the data team.

Replaced YOLO detection plus hand-written rules with graph-based scoring. YOLOv8 extracts component centres, sizes, angles and classes; assembly constraints connect them into a graph, and a graph convolutional network predicts installation and step-completion states.
Models reached around 90% accuracy in internal acceptance testing. Human co-invigilation and tablet scoring provided a fallback so an algorithm failure would not interrupt an exam.

projects.name: coding-agent-from-scratch
projects.subtitle: A terminal coding agent, built from first principles
projects.summary: A command-line coding assistant built without an agent framework. Repository maps, sandbox escape tests and A/A controls put each design decision to the test.
highlights: A native tool-calling ReAct loop with seven tools. SEARCH/REPLACE editing uses a four-tier matching chain to handle whitespace and partial-line drift. Shell commands run inside macOS Seatbelt, with boundaries verified by escape tests: about 1,300 lines of core code and 52 tests, including nine escape tests.

The repository map uses tree-sitter definitions and references to build a file graph, then personalized PageRank to rank context for the task. Constraining edges by actual Python imports raised edge precision from 32% to 100% without dropping a true edge. IDF-weighted seeds addressed query understanding.
On a 112-file repository, the map reduced task steps by 21% and input tokens by 33%. These figures describe that controlled experiment, not a guarantee across repositories.

The evaluation harness runs an A/A arm by default, putting effects beside their noise floor; this led me to retract an earlier claim. In this architecture, output caps made history compression unnecessary. Sub-agent isolation used 42% more total tokens for 22% less main-loop context, without improving completion or correctness. Committed traces make the measurements reproducible.

projects.name: bodycraft-oss
projects.subtitle: Multi-path retrieval with measured scoring weights
projects.summary: Five retrieval paths, visible score breakdowns and repeatable experiments replace opaque weighting with a measurable ranking problem.
highlights: Runs filename and path, section title, SQLite FTS5, dense-vector and entity-graph retrieval in parallel. Four independent weighting strategies score the results, which merge per file with per-path scores exposed.

Moves hard-coded scoring parameters into hot-reloadable configuration. Files the model actually opens provide weak relevance labels, with provenance recorded so they are not mistaken for human annotations.

Optimizes NDCG rather than ratio-style metrics that can improve by collapsing weight onto a single path while the ranking worsens. Grid search maps the space; repeated independent genetic-algorithm runs separate gains from noise.
Index schemas, configuration and ranking metrics are covered by 17 tests. The pipeline runs offline without an API key.

projects.name: Internal spreadsheet Q&A platform
projects.subtitle: Conversational spreadsheet analysis
projects.summary: Turns natural-language questions over uploaded spreadsheets into verified SQL, result tables and charts. Structured plans, whitelisted actions and role-based isolation define what the system can execute.
highlights: A FastAPI and SQLAlchemy backend spans 76 modules, 23,331 lines and 56 test files, using MySQL, Redis, MinIO and Qwen. A 7,487-line React 19 front end streams over SSE. Rolled out to 20+ internal pilot users, whose trial feedback estimated roughly two hours of manual work saved per person per day.

Refactored a fixed LLM workflow into a Planner–Executor design. The planner emits only a structured plan: intent, target fields, actions, constraints and failure policy. The executor runs whitelisted actions over read-only SQL with table, field and permission checks.
Persists session context, generated SQL and chart configuration so follow-up questions can refer to earlier turns. Data isolation follows organization and role boundaries.

Co-authored the invention disclosure, filed in June 2026 and under examination. The pre-execution gate is S = 0.35F + 0.25A + 0.20C + 0.10P + 0.10R, with access compliance A a hard gate. Later rebuilt the core as a native tool in an open-source agent runtime, exposing only a controlled clarify / result_table / result_chart protocol.
